idea.name: Voskll shop-skills classes and camps
idea.one_liner: Teach children woodworking and practical shop skills through parties, classes, camps and group contracts; parents, homeschool groups and institutions pay per student or by contract.
idea.customer: Parents and homeschool families, co-ops, private schools, scholarship-program families, and some event organizers; adult DIY classes and corporate events are requested extensions.
idea.offer: In-person woodworking and shop-skills instruction for children, including birthday events, recurring classes, camps and group contracts; occasional adult DIY and corporate workshops.
idea.revenue_model: Per-child hourly or event fees, camp fees, and group contracts; some state scholarship payments.

acquisition_channels.details: Mike started with a post on his personal Facebook profile, then posted regularly on Facebook and shared class photos.
He posted in homeschool and mothers' Facebook groups and says he is in three homeschool groups.
Mike says the business became word of mouth in the homeschool community.
He became a Step Up scholarship-program vendor and received school and co-op inquiries; he also approached Milwaukee for tool sponsorship.
The business added a Google profile and website; the transcript does not describe search performance.

ideas.delivery: Mike, his wife and occasional helpers teach in person at Voskll's shop or travel with tools and project kits to homes, schools, parks and group venues. They run safety briefings, supervise hands-on builds, and provide camps and contract classes.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR would apply to children's student records and identifiable photos; parent/guardian permissions and careful handling of student data are relevant. The transcript describes no subscription product or employment-agency activity, so DMCC Act subscription rules and Employment Agencies Regs 2003 do not appear central. Cold LinkedIn outreach to individuals for sponsorship would need separate PECR consideration in the UK.
